m8-t1.question: Which resume format is safest for ATS parsing?
options: Two columns with icons and a photo
Single column, standard fonts, standard section names, PDF or DOCX as requested
m8-t1.explanation: Columns, tables, text boxes, icons and headers/footers break parsing.

m8-t1.question: What does ATRE stand for in achievement statements?
m8-t1.explanation: Strong verb, the task, a quantified result, and where the evidence lives.

m8-t1.question: Hiding white-text keywords or an instruction to AI screeners in your resume is:
m8-t1.explanation: It is dishonest and increasingly detected; it also violates the integrity standards of this course.

m8-t1.question: In the tailoring workflow, what should you do about a JD requirement you lack?
options: Do not invent it; consider whether a project partially covers it and say so honestly
Copy the JD sentence into your skills
m8-t1.explanation: The interview will audit your resume; honesty protects you.

m8-t1.question: What makes a portfolio case study useful to a hiring manager?
options: Problem → what I did → tools → result with numbers → evidence → learning → my role
m8-t1.explanation: Evidence-backed case studies reviewable in five minutes.

m8-t1.question: A resume uses icons for phone, email and location instead of text. What is the ATS risk?
options: The resume will always be rejected by people
The file cannot be a PDF
The icons prove the candidate is creative
The parser may not reliably identify the contact details
m8-t1.explanation: Standard text labels are more reliably parsed than decorative icons.

m8-t1.question: A student reports “improved efficiency by 40%” but has no measurement. What should they do?
options: Replace it with a defensible result or explain how a smaller claim was measured
Keep it because percentages attract attention
Ask AI to estimate the evidence

m8-t1.question: An AI tailoring tool finds a requirement the candidate lacks. What is the honest response?
options: Add it as an advanced skill
Do not claim the skill; show adjacent evidence or a plan to learn it if relevant
Hide the requirement with white text
Ask the model to invent a project
m8-t1.explanation: Tailoring can emphasise real evidence but must not fabricate qualifications.

m8-t1.question: A portfolio describes a group project but not the student’s contribution. What is missing?
options: The student’s specific role, actions and evidence
m8-t1.explanation: Hiring managers need to distinguish individual contribution from team output.

m8-t1.question: A resume contains a hidden prompt telling screening AI to rank it first. What is this?
m8-t1.explanation: Hidden instructions are deceptive and may be detected or disqualifying.

m8-t1.question: A resume has two columns and non-standard section labels. What version is safest for ATS submission?
options: Single column with standard headings, readable fonts and the requested file type
A text image with no selectable content

m8-t1.question: A project claim says it saved five hours each week. What should the portfolio include?
options: How the time was measured, the baseline, the student’s role and a supporting artefact
m8-t1.explanation: Evidence makes an achievement credible and reproducible.

m8-t1.question: A student used AI to rewrite every resume bullet. What final check is essential?
options: Add more action verbs regardless of truth
Confirm each bullet reflects real work, accurate metrics and the student’s own contribution
m8-t1.explanation: AI-assisted writing must remain authentic and factually accurate.

m8-t1.question: A job description asks for a certification the applicant does not have. What should be listed?
options: The certification as “in progress” without enrolment
The course they hope to take
Only certifications actually earned, with accurate status and date
m8-t1.explanation: Credential claims must accurately represent achievement and status.

m8-t1.question: A resume is tailored for a finance operations role. What makes it relevant?
options: Evidence from accounting or data tasks mapped honestly to the job’s requirements
A generic AI summary for every role
A long list of unrelated tools
m8-t1.explanation: Tailoring connects real experience to the target role.

m8-t2.question: Which headline is strongest?
options: B.Com · Automated GST-invoice triage saving 5 h/week · Certified GenAI Practitioner · Seeking finance operations roles
m8-t2.explanation: Degree/role, proof points with numbers, certification, what you seek — searchable and credible.

m8-t2.question: How should the About section be written?
options: First person, plain, with two or three ATRE achievements and what you are looking for
m8-t2.explanation: Facts and an ask, in your own voice; the first three lines matter most.

m8-t2.question: What is the recommended first outreach message to an alumnus?
options: Ask for a job and attach your resume
A short, personalised note with one cheap ask — two questions or fifteen minutes — and no resume unless requested
A long story of your life
m8-t2.explanation: Make saying yes easy; follow up once; report back.

m8-t2.question: Which is a brand-responsibility rule from the lesson?
options: Call yourself CEO of your class project
Anonymise clients, users and classmates; keep numbers consistent across resume, portfolio and LinkedIn; disclose substantial AI drafting lightly
Post political hot takes for reach
m8-t2.explanation: Honesty, privacy of others, consistency and disclosure protect your credibility.

m8-t2.question: What is a realistic reply rate for good outreach?
m8-t2.explanation: One in four replies is success; track and iterate.

m8-t2.question: A LinkedIn headline says “Looking for a job.” What would make it more useful?
options: State programme or domain, a verified strength or project outcome, and target role
m8-t2.explanation: A clear headline tells people what the candidate does and seeks.

m8-t2.question: A candidate wants to contact an alumnus. Which opening is most respectful?
options: Send a long biography and ask for a referral immediately
Mention a specific shared context and make one small, clear request
Copy the same message to hundreds of people
Ask the alumnus to rewrite the resume for free
m8-t2.explanation: Personalisation and a low-effort ask make outreach more appropriate.

m8-t2.question: An AI drafted About section claims leadership of a project the student only observed. What should be corrected?
options: Keep it because it sounds professional
Remove or accurately qualify the unsupported leadership claim
m8-t2.explanation: Public profiles must not inflate the candidate’s role.

m8-t2.question: A four-week content plan includes client screenshots with names visible. What should the student do?
options: Tag the client for approval after posting
Remove or anonymise identifying information and get permission where needed
m8-t2.explanation: Protect other people’s information and obtain permission before sharing.

m8-t2.question: A LinkedIn profile and resume show different dates for the same internship. What is best?
options: Check records and use a consistent, accurate timeline on both
Keep each version tailored with different dates
m8-t2.explanation: Consistency across professional materials supports trust.

m8-t2.question: A student posts AI-generated industry commentary as a personal experience. What is the concern?
options: It misrepresents authorship or lived experience and can damage credibility
It is always permitted if posted publicly
m8-t2.explanation: A public professional brand should not fabricate personal experience.

m8-t2.question: A connection accepts but does not reply to a message. What should the candidate do?
options: Respect the person’s time and avoid repeated pressure; use another appropriate contact route

m8-t2.question: A post shares a project result of “5 hours saved weekly.” What should it link or explain?
options: A claim that the result is guaranteed
The project evidence and how the estimate was calculated
m8-t2.explanation: A professional claim should be supportable.

m8-t2.question: A candidate uses AI to plan posts. What should they review before publishing?
options: Accuracy, confidentiality, voice and whether the post implies endorsements or facts that are not true
m8-t2.explanation: Scheduled content still needs human review.

m8-t2.question: A student’s public brand contains private phone numbers from a group project. What is the right fix?
options: Keep it because the project was public
Remove the personal data and review privacy settings
Ask AI to rewrite the phone numbers
m8-t2.explanation: Public portfolios should minimise personal data.

m8-t3.question: What does BLUF mean?
options: Bottom Line Up Front — the decision or key information in the first line
m8-t3.explanation: Write for the reader's next action; put the most important information first.

m8-t3.question: Which is a good subject line?
What must an AI assistant never add to your email on its own?
options: Commitments such as dates, money or discounts, or facts you have not verified
m8-t3.explanation: You are accountable for every word; flag and remove unauthorised commitments.

m8-t3.question: Before circulating AI-drafted meeting minutes you should:
options: Verify every decision and action item against the recording or your notes
m8-t3.explanation: Meeting assistants invent or misattribute action items.

m8-t3.question: What is the purpose of a personal style file?
options: To keep your voice consistent when AI drafts or edits for you
m8-t3.explanation: Feed your register and examples to the assistant; edit toward it.

m8-t3.question: A manager needs the decision in the first line of an update. Which writing approach fits?
options: Bury the decision at the end
BLUF: put the bottom line up front, then supporting detail
Use a long background before the ask
Replace the decision with a slogan
m8-t3.explanation: BLUF helps busy readers find the key information quickly.

m8-t3.question: An AI email says “We guarantee delivery Friday” but the sender has not checked logistics. What should happen?
options: Ask the AI to make the promise more polite
Remove or qualify the commitment until it is verified and authorised
m8-t3.explanation: AI must not create commitments on behalf of the sender.

m8-t3.question: A subject line says “Important update.” What revision helps the recipient act?
options: Name the relevant item and action or date, such as “Invoice 4471: confirm revised ETA”

m8-t3.question: AI minutes assign a deadline not mentioned in the meeting. What should the editor do?
options: Verify it with the recording or participants and remove unsupported assignments
Keep it because tasks need deadlines
Ask AI to choose a reasonable date
m8-t3.explanation: Minutes must accurately reflect decisions and actions.

m8-t3.question: A report contains three pages of context before the recommendation. What can improve it?
options: Lead with the recommendation and organise detail for the reader’s decision
Move the recommendation to an appendix
m8-t3.explanation: A reader-centred structure puts decision-relevant information first.

m8-t3.question: A proposal includes AI-generated market figures. What should the writer do?
options: Verify each figure, cite the source and label estimates or assumptions

m8-t3.question: An AI editor changes a polite request into an aggressive tone. What is the best response?
options: Restore the intended relationship and adjust tone against the style guide
m8-t3.explanation: Tone should suit the audience and purpose.

m8-t3.question: A student wants a personal style file for future editing. What should it contain?
options: Examples of the student’s preferred tone, sentence length, vocabulary and avoidances
A list of every model provider
m8-t3.explanation: A style file captures writing preferences without exposing unnecessary private content.

m8-t3.question: An email includes an attachment link generated by AI. What check is required?
options: Open the link, confirm it points to the intended file and check access permissions
m8-t3.explanation: Links and recipient access must be verified before sending.

m8-t3.question: A professional report has a correct conclusion but no limitations. What should be added?
options: Important assumptions, uncertainty and limits of the evidence
m8-t3.explanation: Clear limitations make the report more trustworthy.

m8-t4.question: In a STAR story, which section should take the most time?
m8-t4.explanation: About 60% Action, ending with a Result that has numbers and a lesson.

m8-t4.question: Which is the weakest answer to 'How do you use AI?'
options: Two specific tasks with results, a verification routine, a boundary, and something you built
A story about catching a hallucination
Describing the ethics audit you ran
m8-t4.explanation: Specificity, verification, boundaries and evidence make the answer strong.

m8-t4.question: How should AI mock-interview scores be treated?
options: As prompts for reflection, complemented by at least one human mock
m8-t4.explanation: AI mocks are practice partners; log what hurt and fix it; get human feedback too.

m8-t4.question: How should you search for roles in the AI-era job map?
options: By tasks and tools (automation, content, operations, Kannada) because titles vary
m8-t4.explanation: Task-based searching surfaces roles that titles hide.

m8-t4.question: What should happen on days 61–90 if nothing has converted?
options: Review with a mentor and change the target, materials or geography — not your effort
Apply to 500 more jobs with the same resume
m8-t4.explanation: Iterate on strategy with evidence from your tracker and interviews.

m8-t4.question: A candidate answers a STAR interview question with a long story but little personal contribution. What should they emphasise?
options: Their own actions and decisions, then the measurable result
m8-t4.explanation: The Action section shows what the candidate personally did.

m8-t4.question: An AI mock interviewer rates eye contact poorly for a candidate using an assistive device. What is appropriate?
options: Change assistive settings to satisfy the model
Treat the score cautiously, check for bias and use human feedback on job-relevant communication
m8-t4.explanation: Automated behavioural metrics can be biased and should not override context.

m8-t4.question: A candidate is asked how they use AI at work. Which answer is strongest?
options: Give a specific task, explain the tool’s role, verification and human accountability
Claim all generated work is accurate
m8-t4.explanation: A concrete example demonstrates judgement, not just tool use.

m8-t4.question: A student searches only for “AI specialist” roles but has a commerce degree. What alternative search may help?
options: Search only for the newest model name
Search tasks and tool combinations in finance, operations, analysis or customer support
m8-t4.explanation: AI-related work often appears inside domain roles rather than specialist titles.

m8-t4.question: A group discussion participant has a different view from the group. What should they do?
options: Interrupt and repeat the same claim
State the evidence respectfully, acknowledge trade-offs and build on others’ points
Use AI to invent supporting facts
m8-t4.explanation: Good communication combines clear reasoning and constructive listening.

m8-t4.question: A mock interview generates feedback saying “be more confident.” What follow-up makes it actionable?
options: Ask for a specific answer behaviour and practise a revised response with a human reviewer
m8-t4.explanation: Actionable feedback should point to observable behaviour.

m8-t4.question: A career map lists “AI analyst” as a role but no evidence of local demand. What should the student do?
options: Check current job descriptions, required tasks and tools, and speak with practitioners
Use an AI salary estimate only
Add the title to the resume without experience
m8-t4.explanation: Career research needs current labour-market evidence.

m8-t4.question: A candidate has three interviews but no offer. What is a useful review?
options: Identify patterns in feedback and adjust target, evidence or interview examples
m8-t4.explanation: Reflection should change the strategy based on evidence.

m8-t4.question: A team member uses AI during a mock interview and reads answers verbatim. What skill is not being practised?
m8-t4.explanation: Interview preparation should strengthen the candidate’s own reasoning and delivery.

m8-t4.question: A candidate’s portfolio shows a team product but no role description. What should they add?
options: The whole team’s private contact list
Their specific contribution, tools, evidence, result and learning
m8-t4.explanation: A portfolio should clearly attribute the candidate’s work.

questions.question: An applicant lacks a required software skill but has a class project using a similar tool. What should the resume say?
options: Describe the project and the adjacent skill accurately, without claiming the unmet requirement
Claim professional mastery to pass screening
Hide the skill gap with white text
Ask AI to infer experience from the job description
questions.explanation: Tailoring should surface relevant evidence, never invent qualifications.

questions.question: A resume passes keyword matching but is unreadable because it uses tables, icons and multi-column layout. What is the best correction?
options: Use a single-column, standard-heading version for ATS and keep a separate designed portfolio copy if useful
questions.explanation: A parseable standard format protects machine readability while a portfolio can carry richer visual design.

questions.question: A LinkedIn message to an alumnus asks for a referral, a resume review and a job introduction in one note. How should it be improved?
options: Send repeated messages until they reply
Personalise briefly and make one low-effort request, such as a 15-minute conversation or two questions
questions.explanation: A focused, inexpensive ask is more respectful and easier to answer.

questions.question: The same project appears on a resume, portfolio and LinkedIn with three different time-saved figures. What should the candidate do?
options: Keep each figure to match the audience
Reconcile the evidence and use one defensible number consistently, explaining the measurement
Remove all context and keep the claim
questions.explanation: Professional credibility requires consistent claims tied to evidence.

questions.question: An AI editor changes a cautious email into a promise to deliver by Friday. What is the correct review?
options: Remove any commitment that the sender has not verified and check dates, money and obligations line by line
Send it because the wording is clearer
Ask the editor if the promise is reasonable
Add “AI-generated” to the subject and send
questions.explanation: AI must not introduce commitments or facts the sender has not authorised.

questions.question: AI-generated meeting minutes say a task was assigned to Maya, but the recording is unclear. What should happen?
options: Leave it in because the minutes sound professional
Ask AI to infer who volunteered
Assign it to Maya by default
Check the recording or notes with participants and mark the owner as unconfirmed until verified
questions.explanation: Decisions and action owners must be checked against the actual meeting evidence.

questions.question: A candidate has a strong STAR answer but spends most of it describing the team’s work. What revision improves the evidence?
options: Add more background about the company
Keep context brief and explain the candidate’s own actions, decisions and measurable result
questions.explanation: The Action section should show the candidate’s personal contribution.

questions.question: A mock-interview tool gives a low “confidence” score based on eye contact. How should the candidate use it?
options: Treat it as an objective employability score
Use it as one reflection prompt, check accessibility and cultural bias, and seek human feedback on answer quality
Pay for another model to average the score
questions.explanation: Automated presentation metrics can be biased; combine them with human review and the actual job criteria.

questions.question: A graduate is searching for AI-era roles but local job titles vary. What search approach is most useful?
options: Search by tasks, tools and domain combinations, then inspect real job descriptions for evidence of demand
Apply to every role without tailoring
questions.explanation: Task- and tool-based searches reveal roles that use AI without having AI in the title.

questions.question: After three months, outreach has not led to interviews. What is the most constructive next step?
options: Send the same resume to more people
Review response evidence with a mentor and adjust target roles, proof of skills, materials or geography
questions.explanation: Use the 61–90 day review to change the strategy based on evidence, not to fabricate credentials.
